source: Traced by hand and by color from USGS NAIP aerial photos (public domain), to fill in what OpenStreetMap doesn't have yet.

unsure.all: no hole map found and the photo doesn't show the order: I took the 9 greens east of the canal as the front nine and the 9 west of it as the back, and numbered each nine as a walking loop that fits the card's pars and lengths
unsure.7: back tee placed at the east end of the strip under trees; the visible tee pads are about 90 m closer, which would make it a par-3 length
unsure.12: tee placed on the narrow strip by the canal, sharing it with hole 10
unsure.18: old tee sat on the canal bank; moved to the open fairway south of the lake by the 17th green. The photo shows only the straight strip beside the canal, no lake to bend sharply round, so the shape is one gentle bend; tee and corridor overlap hole 13 and the order here is a guess
unsure.9: long walk to this tee and from this green to the 10th tee; order here is a guess
unsure.2: bend placed where the fairway passes south of the trees short of the green; the tee pads are not clear
